guidance_for_write_dockerfile_agent: The Dockerfile build fails at the step where 'update-alternatives' tries to set /usr/bin/python to /usr/bin/python3.9. The error is: 'update-alternatives: error: alternative path /usr/bin/python3.9 doesn't exist'. This indicates that python3.9 is not installed at /usr/bin/python3.9 in the base Ubuntu 22.04 image, or the package python3.9 is not available under that name in the apt repository used. Ubuntu 22.04 defaults to python3.10, so python3.9 may not be present by that name. To fix, either adjust the Dockerfile to use the default python3 interpreter (likely python3.10) by setting update-alternatives to /usr/bin/python3 instead of python3.9, or explicitly install python3.9 from an alternative source or PPA if that exact version is strictly required. Alternatively, remove the 'update-alternatives' step if not necessary and rely on python3 as default, or update all relevant steps to python3 instead of python3.9. Also verify that conda environment creation uses a python version compatible with the installed system python or adjust accordingly. Fixing this will allow the image to build successfully and the environment to be setup properly before running tests in the evaluation script.
